headline: Forest’s dominant numbers bring only a point at Ipswich

sentences.text: Nottingham Forest left Portman Road with a point, but the 1–1 draw felt like a missed opportunity after a performance that produced far more than the final score suggests.
Neco Williams put Forest ahead in the 13th minute, assisted by Daniel Muñoz, before Julio Enciso levelled for Ipswich in the 41st minute.
That made it 1–1 at the break, and neither side found a second-half goal.
Forest had 50.6% possession and 17 shots to Ipswich’s 7, while the expected-goals figures were 2.29 to 0.46.
They also led 5–3 in shots on target and 5–0 in corners, and created 2 big chances to Ipswich’s 1.
Yet Forest’s 11 attempts off target, alongside 2 blocked shots, underline the frustration: their attacking volume did not become a winning goal.
Ipswich made 5 substitutions and Forest 3 as the game progressed, but the score remained unchanged after the interval.
The point ends Forest’s run of 3 consecutive league defeats, though their previous 5 matches had yielded only 4 points.
Ipswich, by contrast, had collected 6 points from their previous 5 league games before adding this draw.
Forest climbed from 19th before kick-off to 16th, now with 6 points from 8 matches; Ipswich moved from 10th to 9th and have 10 points.
For Forest supporters, the table offers some relief, but the disparity in chances makes this feel like 2 points left behind rather than a point gained.
